name: Horton Social Science Center
use: Social sciences departments (history, political science, sociology/anthropology historically), classrooms, lecture halls
builtText: 1967–68 (opened 1968–69; dedicated Apr 30, 1977); archives index says built 1966
architect: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (New York); builder Harvey Construction
style: Late-1960s modernist: precast concrete grid of deep-set windows

renovations.what: Third floor fully renovated (~$1.5M); second floor done in the prior two summers; seminar rooms got A/C; lecture halls reshaped to bowls
Six summers of phased interior renewal completed: classrooms, offices, labs, first-floor academic commons, new heating terminals, BMS controls, efficient lighting

facts.text: Designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill of New York and built by Harvey Construction in 1967–68; opened for the 1968–69 year.
Dedicated April 30, 1977 to trustee chair Mildred McAfee Horton.
Harriman finished six years of summer renovation phases in 2018 within a $6.1M budget, adding a first-floor academic commons and correcting safety deficiencies.
A faculty member said in 2014 the renovations made a huge difference to quality of life and seminar rooms gained air conditioning.

verdict: SOM's 1968 precast grid for the social sciences: sober and well proportioned, with interiors renewed floor by floor to 2018.
notes: Photos show a four-story tan precast-concrete frame with deep square window bays, a sober SOM modernist block; trees soften it. Built year conflicts: archives narrative 1967–68, archives index "built 1966", TNH 2014 "1966". A/C confirmed only in seminar spaces (2014); whole-building A/C not confirmed. No interior photo; no student reviews found.
judgeNotes: Photos show a disciplined concrete frame behind trees; 02 leads because 01 has construction fencing.
